D003-D008_h024.question:
I’ve always been kind of wound up, even as a kid. Teachers used to send notes home because I couldn’t stay in my seat and was always blurting things out or cutting people off. My mom said I was “go, go, go” from the minute I woke up. That’s never really gone away.

At work now, I’m supposed to sit through safety meetings, but I can’t stay put. I’ll get up, pace in the back, or find some excuse to step out. My legs feel jumpy, like I’ve got to keep moving. Even on my days off, my wife says I can’t just sit and watch a movie—I’m up changing lightbulbs, checking the basement, anything.

I have a hard time sticking with one task. I’ll start cleaning one floor, then something catches my eye and I wander off to another job, and I forget to finish the first one. Keeping my supplies and schedule straight is a mess; I lose track of what I was doing all the time.

Sometimes my mood lifts and I feel unusually upbeat or irritable for a few days, but this restlessness and butting into people’s conversations is there whether my mood is up, down, or just normal.
D003-D008_h024.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D003-D008_h025.question:
I’ve always been kind of wired. Even as a kid, I got in trouble for not staying in my seat and blurting things out in class. My parents used to say I was “go, go, go” all the time. That hasn’t really changed. I’m 42 now, in design meetings I’ll get up and pace or start sketching on the wall because I just can’t sit still through a whole session. My legs are bouncing constantly; I feel like I have this motor running inside me.

I cut people off a lot—colleagues, clients, even my wife—because thoughts pop into my head and I jump in before they’re done. At home, I’ll start reorganizing the living room in the middle of a conversation or wander off while my wife is talking.

Focusing on plans and drawings is hard unless there’s a tight deadline. I’ll drift off halfway through emails or zoning regulations, and my desk is a mess of half-finished sketches and notes. I struggle to structure projects, so I’m always juggling things last minute.

Every now and then I’ll have a few days where I feel unusually upbeat and energized, sleep less, take on extra projects—but the restlessness and impulsive stuff are there all the time, not just during those “up” periods.
D003-D008_h025.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder
    B. Delusional Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
